+[package]
+name = "camcraft-simview"
+description = "The stand-alone camcraft-sim program: replays a CLFile or a posted 3-axis G-code file against stock, tools, a machine file and a post manifest, headless. No world, no entities, no UI. Clean-room implementation, public sources only."
+version.workspace = true
+edition.workspace = true
+rust-version.workspace = true
+
+# One binary, two subcommands (`cl`, `check`). The name is the one the
+# sim crate's binary had: two binaries with one name collide in target/.
+[[bin]]
+name = "camcraft-sim"
+path = "src/main.rs"
+
+[dependencies]
+# Edges and their imported items: docs/decisions/2574-standalone-camcraft-sim.md.
+camcraft-gcode = { workspace = true }
+camcraft-post = { workspace = true }
+camcraft-sim = { workspace = true }
+tracing-subscriber = { workspace = true }

@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+## #2574 - A stand-alone camcraft-sim (research decisions, carried by #2586)
+
+The research of #2574 used no branch. Its answers are in the issue
+comments of 2026-11-18. This file records the decisions, as the research
+asked, in the first code slice (#2586).
+
+**The layout.** A new crate `crates/simview`, package `camcraft-simview`,
+holds the binary `camcraft-sim`. It does not depend on `camcraft-app` or
+`camcraft-ui`: a stand-alone program that builds the document engine
+(flecs) is not stand-alone, and it shares the crash domain of the app. The
+generated machine model is in `camcraft-sim` (#2584); the part tree type is
+in `camcraft-post::machine` (#2583); the per-move limit judgment moved to
+`camcraft-post` (#2585). `camcraft-sim` gets no `post` edge: `simview` maps
+the tree into the model's own input types.
+- Dropped: the viewer inside `camcraft-ui` (it pulls flecs and the
+  document); the viewer inside `camcraft-sim` (that crate is data only).
+
+**The old binary.** `crates/sim/src/bin/camcraft-sim.rs` moved into the new
+crate as the subcommand `camcraft-sim cl <file.cl> ...`, with the same
+arguments, output and exit codes. Two binaries with one name in one
+workspace collide in `target/`. It was not in the release packages, so no
+user loses it.
+
+**The process launch (#2589, later slice).** CamCraft starts `camcraft-sim`
+as a separate process (`std::process::Command`), found beside
+`std::env::current_exe()`. A missing binary disables the button with a
+named reason. Dropped: a shared window in the app process (it ties the
+viewer to the flecs build and the app's crash domain).
+
+**The file contract for Solidcraft (#2593, research).** A file, not a live
+MCP call: the machine assembly is exported one time as URDF, and the `.mch`
+names it and maps each URDF joint to an axis letter. `camcraft-sim` reads
+only the file. Dropped: a live MCP call (a runtime dependency on another
+process); a reader of the `.sc` document's joints (it couples CamCraft to
+Solidcraft's document version).
+
+**The `body` key layers (#2591, later slice).** One optional key on a
+`.mch` part, in three layers: no `body` gives the generated model (#2584);
+`body.primitives` gives boxes, cylinders and cones in the part frame;
+`body.step` names a STEP file read by the solidcore reader. Each finding and
+each pass on a generated body says "judged on a generated model". Dropped: a
+separate definition language for the primitives.
+
+**The exit codes.** 0: each check ran and passed. 1: bad input. 2: a check
+failed (each finding names its NC line). 3: one or more checks were not
+judged (each is named). A check that did not run never reads as a pass, and
+2 wins over 3.
+
+**The crate edges of `camcraft-simview`** (AGENTS.md "No new dependency
+between our crates without a decision"). `camcraft-sim` is a binary: it is
+the top caller, and it must read the files itself. No caller can pass the
+values in.
+- `camcraft-gcode`: `parse_with`, `ParseOptions`, `ReferencePositions`,
+  `Dialect` and its seven profiles (`rs274`, `fanuc`, `haas`, `tormach`,
+  `grblhal`, `tinyg`, `carvera`), `ParsedSection` (`tool_number`,
+  `work_offset`, `toolpath`, `move_lines`), `WorkOffset::number`, and the
+  text of `GcodeError`.
+- `camcraft-post`: `machine::{parse_mch, parse_mch_tree, kind, Kind,
+  Machine, MachineTree, TreePart, PartKind, MovingSide, MachineCheck,
+  SourceLocation}` and `post::{engine::extension_of,
+  dialect::declared_serves, js::Script, work_offset::work_offsets,
+  PostError}`.
+- `camcraft-sim`: `stock_sim::{Stock, Backend, SimOp, auto_cell,
+  FIELD_BAND}`, `verify::{bands_vs_fixtures, rapids_vs_fixtures, Warning,
+  FixturePart}`, `fixture::FixtureBox`, `tools::ToolGeom`,
+  `machine_model::{generate, Body, BodyKind, BodySource, JointKind,
+  MachineSpec, PartSpec, SpindleSpec, ToolStationSpec}`, and its re-exports
+  `cl::{Move, MoveKind, Toolpath, text}`, `geometry::{Point3, Triangle}`,
+  `geo2d::Point2`.
+- No direct edge to `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-cl` or `camcraft-tools`
+  (the research listed them): each type that `simview` uses comes through
+  the re-exports of `camcraft-sim`, so a direct edge adds nothing.
+- What rebuilds: `camcraft-simview` rebuilds when `gcode`, `post` or `sim`
+  (and below them `cl`, `geometry`, `tools`, `kernel`) change. No crate
+  depends on `camcraft-simview`: a change in it rebuilds only itself.
+- `camcraft-sim` drops its `tracing-subscriber` dependency: only the moved
+  binary used it.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Low for the layout (one binary crate, no
+dependants). The exit codes are a contract for scripts and for the
+"Simulate" button: change them only with a breaking note.

+## #2586 - camcraft-sim check: what each check judges, and what it names as not judged
+
+Decisions taken unattended while the first slice of #2574 was written.
+
+**The limits are judged in program coordinates.** A `.mch` stroke is in
+PROGRAM coordinates (`assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, `travel`; #2574 answer 3).
+The NC moves are program coordinates, so the #2585 check runs with a zero
+origin and needs no `--wcs`. A stroke that the file does not state is named
+"not judged" (the check itself skips it in silence). Dropped: judging
+`work + --wcs` against the stroke (that frame is not the file's).
+
+**`--wcs` is for the machine model and the frames.** The machine-part
+collision poses the model at `work + origin`; an offset with no `--wcs`
+names its lines as not judged. The stock and the fixtures are in the frame
+of the first section's offset; a section in another offset is moved by the
+difference of the two origins, or named as not judged.
+
+**G28 and G30 go to machine zero.** That is the reference point of a control
+that states no other (the Fanuc default). In an offset with no `--wcs`, a
+G28, G30 or G53 move has no known work position: the parser gets a
+stand-in origin so that it completes, and each such move (and the move
+after it) is skipped by each check and named ("reference moves", exit 3).
+Dropped: a refusal of each program that uses G28 with no `--wcs` (most
+posted programs end with G28); a guessed home.
+
+**The first move: only its end is judged.** The program does not say where
+the machine stands at its start. The report says so in a note. Dropped:
+the parser's guess (the work origin) as the start, which can read a
+diagonal rapid through the stock; a "not judged" for each program.
+
+**The rapid law reads the simulated stock.** A rapid fails when its tip disc
+(the centre, and eight points at the radius less one cell) is more than one
+cell deep in the material that is left before the rapid. Dropped: the
+geometric law of `cl` (each rapid under the stock top inside the
+footprint), which flags a rapid into a pocket that an earlier move cut.
+
+**No "cut under the stock bottom" in `check`.** The catalog program drills
+through the stock bottom, which is legal. What stands under the stock is
+judged by the fixture law and the machine model. The `cl` subcommand keeps
+its old verdict unchanged.
+
+**The holder law reads the simulated stock move by move.** The shank band
+(when the T map states a shank) and the holder band must not be more than
+one cell deep in the material that is left before the move. `verify`'s
+region-based shank law is per operation: on a whole program it reads stock
+that earlier operations cut, and it over-reports. To keep the cost low, the
+moves are cut in batches, and each move is probed on the stock before its
+batch. Material only goes, so a clean probe on that stock is clean on the
+exact stock; a suspected hit cuts the batch and probes again. The verdict is
+the move-by-move verdict. A tool with no `flute=` and `holder=` is named as
+not judged.
+
+**The fixture law is `verify`'s region-free law.** `bands_vs_fixtures` and
+`rapids_vs_fixtures` over `--fixture` boxes. With no `--fixture`, the line
+says "no fixture is stated" and passes: the program cannot know of a
+fixture that the user does not state.
+
+**The machine model.** The tree maps to `MachineSpec`: a linear part drives
+the letter of its `name` (else its `id`); a table-side part runs against
+the program axis; a rotary is posed at zero. The spindle side is a head and
+each axis whose moving side is the tool; the work side is each other
+`Block` body. The tool envelope is not steel and is not judged. Bodies are
+tested with the separating axis theorem (each body is convex), at poses
+about 2 mm apart along each move, with a 0.01 mm touch tolerance. In the
+generated model, joint zero puts the spindle nose on the table top
+(#2584).
+
+**Inputs.** The dialect comes from `--dialect`, else from the post's file
+name when it is a built-in profile name (`fanuc.cps` gives `fanuc`); else
+the run refuses. A post with no `serves` serves milling. A machine that is
+not a mill refuses (this slice is 3-axis milling). A T number that the
+program uses and `--tools` does not state refuses (exit 1, the rule of
+#2213). A `.camtools` file refuses by name: its reader is in `camcraft-app`
+and it states no T numbers (#4465). The stock is the field engine with the
+`auto_cell` of the smallest tool, or `--cell`.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Each law is one module of `crates/simview/src/check/`
+with its own pins in `crates/simview/tests/check/`.
